```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## 1. Aim

Install the R packages needed for data import, then import data from:

1. Text files (TXT, CSV)
2. Excel
3. Statistical packages (SPSS, Stata, SAS)
4. Other text formats (JSON, XML, web scraping)
5. Database management systems (SQLite, with notes for MySQL, Oracle and Access)

For each source, we show how the package helps us look at the data.

## 2. Install and load packages

Run the install line only one time.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("readxl", "writexl", "haven", "foreign",
                   "DBI", "RSQLite", "jsonlite", "xml2", "rvest",
                   "dplyr", "ggplot2"))
```

```{r load}
library(readxl)    # read Excel
library(haven)     # read SPSS, Stata, SAS
library(foreign)   # older SPSS/Stata reader
library(DBI)       # common database interface
library(RSQLite)   # SQLite driver
library(jsonlite)  # JSON
library(xml2)      # XML
library(rvest)     # web scraping
library(dplyr)     # data handling
library(ggplot2)   # graphs
```

Create the sample files (same 20 students saved in many formats):

```{r make-data}
source("data/make_sample_data.R")
list.files("data")
```

## 3. Text files

### 3.1 TXT file (class data from the lecture)

```{r txt}
data_class <- read.table("data/class_data.txt", header = TRUE)
head(data_class)
summary(data_class)
```

### 3.2 CSV file

```{r csv}
csv_data <- read.csv("data/students.csv")
str(csv_data)
```

## 4. Excel

`readxl` reads `.xlsx` and `.xls` files without needing Excel installed.

```{r excel}
excel_sheets("data/students.xlsx")
excel_data <- read_excel("data/students.xlsx", sheet = 1)
head(excel_data)
```

## 5. Statistical packages (SAS, SPSS, Stata)

`haven` keeps variable labels and value labels from these programs.

### 5.1 SPSS (.sav)

```{r spss}
spss_data <- read_sav("data/students.sav")
head(spss_data)

# The older 'foreign' package can also read SPSS
spss_data2 <- read.spss("data/students.sav", to.data.frame = TRUE)
dim(spss_data2)
```

### 5.2 Stata (.dta)

```{r stata}
stata_data <- read_dta("data/students.dta")
summary(stata_data$math_score)
```

### 5.3 SAS (.xpt / .sas7bdat)

```{r sas}
sas_data <- read_xpt("data/students.xpt")
head(sas_data)
# For a .sas7bdat file use:  read_sas("file.sas7bdat")
```

## 6. JSON, XML and web scraping

### 6.1 JSON

```{r json}
json_data <- fromJSON("data/students.json")
head(json_data)
```

### 6.2 XML

```{r xml}
doc <- read_xml("data/students.xml")
nodes <- xml_find_all(doc, "//student")
xml_data <- data.frame(
  id         = as.integer(xml_text(xml_find_first(nodes, "id"))),
  gender     = xml_text(xml_find_first(nodes, "gender")),
  math_score = as.numeric(xml_text(xml_find_first(nodes, "math_score")))
)
head(xml_data)
```

### 6.3 Web scraping (needs internet)

```{r scrape, eval=FALSE}
page   <- read_html("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda")
tables <- html_table(page, fill = TRUE)
head(tables[[2]])
```

## 7. Database management systems

### 7.1 SQLite (works without a server)

```{r sqlite}
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "data/school.db")
dbListTables(con)

# Simple query
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM students LIMIT 5")

# Query with JOIN and GROUP BY, done inside the database
dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT s.program, c.faculty,
         COUNT(*)              AS n_students,
         ROUND(AVG(s.math_score), 1) AS avg_math
  FROM students s
  JOIN courses c ON s.program = c.program
  GROUP BY s.program, c.faculty
")

db_data <- dbReadTable(con, "students")
dbDisconnect(con)
```

### 7.2 MySQL, Oracle and MS Access (same DBI idea)

Only the connection line changes. Server details below are examples.

```{r other-db, eval=FALSE}
# MySQL
library(RMySQL)
con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host = "localhost", dbname = "school",
                 user = "root", password = Sys.getenv("MYSQL_PWD"))

# Oracle or MS Access through ODBC
library(odbc)
con <- dbConnect(odbc(), dsn = "MyOracleDSN")
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
  .connection_string = "Driver={Microsoft Access Driver (*.mdb, *.accdb)};DBQ=C:/data/school.accdb;")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM students")
dbDisconnect(con)
```

## 8. How the libraries help on the imported data

All sources give the same data frame, so we can use one set of tools on any of them.

```{r compare}
# Same number of rows from each source
sapply(list(csv = csv_data, excel = excel_data, spss = spss_data,
            stata = stata_data, sas = sas_data, json = json_data,
            database = db_data), nrow)
```

```{r dplyr}
# dplyr: summary by group
stata_data %>%
  group_by(program, gender) %>%
  summarise(students = n(),
            mean_math = round(mean(math_score), 1),
            mean_it   = round(mean(it_score), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
# ggplot2: graph of data that came from the database
ggplot(db_data, aes(x = program, y = it_score, fill = program)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "IT score by program (data from SQLite)",
       x = "Program", y = "IT score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r ggplot2, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(spss_data, aes(math_score, it_score, colour = gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Math vs IT score (data from SPSS file)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 9. Summary

| Source | Package | Function |
|---|---|---|
| TXT / CSV | base R | `read.table()`, `read.csv()` |
| Excel | readxl | `read_excel()` |
| SPSS | haven / foreign | `read_sav()`, `read.spss()` |
| Stata | haven | `read_dta()` |
| SAS | haven | `read_xpt()`, `read_sas()` |
| JSON | jsonlite | `fromJSON()` |
| XML | xml2 | `read_xml()` |
| Web page | rvest | `read_html()`, `html_table()` |
| SQLite / MySQL / Oracle / Access | DBI + driver | `dbConnect()`, `dbGetQuery()` |
